filename: Causal inference for process understanding in Earth sciences.pdf
title: Causal inference for process understanding in Earth sciences
testbed_rationale: This paper is a conceptual and methodological overview/perspective on applying Pearlian causal inference, directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), and do-calculus in Earth sciences, accompanied only by a 1D synthetic toy model and conceptual case studies.
pain_points: Incomplete observation / partial observation of the Earth system state space leading to unobserved confounding
Feedbacks creating cycles in causal graphs (addressed by resolving temporal dynamics)
Unidentifiability when backdoor paths cannot be blocked
Observational selection bias (e.g., satellite sampling and cloud masking)
extraction_notes: The paper also mentions the Chilean Coastal Orographic Precipitation Experiment (CCOPE, Massmann et al. 2017) as a conceptual example/case study for constructing causal graphs, but does not use or generate CCOPE data directly within this manuscript.
